findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that verifies the usage_log ticket-attribution fix (e.g. a test asserting eval calls are attributed to the correct ticket).

Child decomposition groups it under criteria 6,7,8, but AC 6 verifies the ledger, AC 7 verifies model-parity — neither mentions the usage-log ticket-attribution bug.
Absence: no AC line references usage_log attribution correctness.
findings.finding: The scope lists "fixes to usage_log ticket attribution" as a deliverable, but no acceptance criterion covers or verifies it.
findings.location: Scope paragraph ("fixes to usage_log ticket attribution") and Acceptance Criteria list
scenarios: A described deliverable ships (or silently does not) with no test/manifest gating its completion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the stratification dimensions and selection rule for the ~20-ticket Tier-2 sample (and how it is frozen in the corpus manifest).
evidence: Approach: "Re-run finders with candidate criteria on a fixed stratified sample (~20 tickets)".
AC 5: "...on a fixed stratified sample..." — the strata (by criterion? verdict? outcome label? store?) are never named.
Signal (1)/(2): sample-selection protocol is a data-design decision left implicit.
findings.finding: The stratified sample (~20 tickets) has no stated stratification dimensions, so the frozen sample is not reproducibly definable.
findings.location: Approach, Tier 2 ("a fixed stratified sample (~20 tickets)") and AC 5
scenarios: Two executors build differently composed 20-ticket samples; Tier-2 results are not comparable across proposals despite the sample being called 'fixed'.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify strata (e.g. stratify by triggered criterion and by verdict class, seeded deterministically, recorded in the manifest).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the noise band is computed from the 208 identical-material flips + Tier-1 reproduction, and the exact comparison that classifies a delta as improve / regress / indistinguishable.
evidence: Invariant 4: "reported as regressing/improving only when its label-proxy deltas exceed the noise band measured from identical-material flips and the Tier-1 reproduction run".
No stated aggregation: is the band a raw count, a proportion, a confidence interval, a multiple of the flip rate? Signal (2): a derived metric with no computation protocol.
findings.finding: The noise-aware acceptance rule references a 'noise band' but does not state how the band is computed into an accept/regress/improve threshold.
scenarios: Two analysts compute the band differently (e.g. std-dev vs percentile) and reach opposite improve/regress verdicts on the same delta.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the band as e.g. a confidence interval on the identical-material flip rate combined with per-question reproduction variance, and state the delta-vs-band comparison rule.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define 'friction rate' (its numerator/denominator and the corpus signal it derives from) in the plan.
evidence: AC 3 lists "friction rate" among diff-report metrics.
Absence: 'friction' is never defined; there is no formula relating it to verdict flips, revise→re-review pairs, or block_threshold. Signal (2): derived metric with no computation.
findings.finding: AC 3 requires reporting a 'friction rate' but no computation or aggregation protocol for it is given anywhere in the plan.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, item 3 ("...label-proxy precision/recall, friction rate...")
scenarios: Implementer invents a friction-rate definition; a later reviewer disputes it and the Tier-0 report is re-derived.
findings.suggested_fix: State e.g. friction rate = fraction of reviews that would flip PASS→BLOCK (extra revise cycles) under the candidate overlay, computed over the corpus.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the parity guard resolves a single reference model when the corpus contains multiple production model ids (e.g. per-pass grouping, or excluding off-baseline sidecars from LLM tiers).
evidence: Invariant 2: "refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's `provider_provenance.ran_model`."
Context: corpus = ~4,300 tree sidecars (2026-06-27→now) + ~2,000 git-recovered + 74 from a separate repo; a window this long across model upgrades can hold heterogeneous ran_model ids.
Contradiction: a single 'corpus baseline' model id is assumed, but the corpus may not have one.
findings.finding: The model-parity guard keys off 'the corpus baseline's provider_provenance.ran_model' (singular), but the corpus spans two stores and a long, partly-pruned time window that plausibly contains more than one production model id, making the guard's reference model ambiguous.
scenarios: Corpus contains Opus-v1 and Opus-v2 sidecars; the guard either blocks all runs or silently compares against one arbitrary baseline, confounding parity.
findings.suggested_fix: Define parity per (pass, model-id) cohort: LLM re-runs only compare against sidecars whose ran_model matches the configured model, and off-baseline sidecars are excluded from that tier's diff.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default handling of v2 sidecars that fail fingerprint reconstruction (e.g. included for Tier-0/label joins on stored data, excluded only from LLM tiers).
evidence: AC 1 allows up to 5% unreconstructed.
Approach: Tier 1 and Tier 2 re-runs require "reconstructed plan text"; the disposition of the unreconstructed remainder is unstated. Signal (2): defaultable gap.
Tier 0 label joins are described as pure functions of the corpus — unclear whether unreconstructed sidecars still contribute their stored decisions/labels.
findings.finding: The plan does not state how the ≤5% of v2 sidecars whose at-review plan text cannot be reconstructed/fingerprint-verified are handled in the corpus and downstream label joins.
findings.location: AC 1 ("...reconstructed and fingerprint-verified for ≥95% of v2 sidecars") and Approach Tier 1/Tier 2 (which need reconstructed plan text)
scenarios: Executor drops the 5% entirely, silently shrinking the label corpus and the noise floor sample.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: unreconstructed sidecars remain in the corpus for Tier-0/label purposes (their stored decisions/labels are intact) but are excluded from Tier-1/Tier-2 LLM re-runs, and the manifest records both counts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct AC #1 (and the Context claim) to describe what material_fingerprint actually proves (normalized material-subset equality, excluding title/checkbox-state/insignificant-whitespace), and state how byte-exact-enough reconstruction is otherwise assured or why normalized equivalence suffices for the model re-runs.
evidence: pass1.material_fingerprint delegates to material_diff.material_basis, which hashes {ticket_id, canonical_description, file_impact, sorted children ids, optional no_file_impact_reason} — a SUBSET of the reviewed material

material_diff.normalize_checkbox_state erases checkbox state and normalize_insignificant_whitespace strips CRLF/trailing-ws/boundary-blank-lines before hashing, so the digest is over a NORMALIZED description, not raw bytes
generation.from_snapshot builds the reviewed PlanContext with `title` (and full `state`), but `title` is absent from material_basis — a differing title would still fingerprint-match
material_fingerprint docstring: 'Tags/comments/links/assignee are NOT material (excluded), and neither is AC checkbox STATE ... nor insignificant whitespace'
findings.finding: AC #1's 'fingerprint-verified byte-exactly against the stored material_fingerprint' overstates what the fingerprint can prove: material_fingerprint hashes a NORMALIZED and PARTIAL basis, so a match does not establish byte-exact reconstruction of the reviewed plan text.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, criterion 1 ('at-review plan text reconstructed and fingerprint-verified byte-exactly'); also Context ('verifiable byte-exactly against the stored material_fingerprint')
scenarios: Two reconstructions differing only in checkbox state, trailing whitespace, line-endings, or title both 'verify' against the same fingerprint, so the harness admits a plan text the reviewer never saw as if byte-exact
The ≥95% coverage metric counts fingerprint matches as byte-exact reconstructions, inflating confidence in corpus fidelity for Tiers 1/2 which feed reconstructed text to the model
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe the verification as 'material-fingerprint-equivalent (normalized basis) for ≥95% of v2 sidecars' and, if byte-exact text matters for Tier-1/2, add an explicit reconstruction-fidelity check over the fields the fingerprint omits (title, checkbox state, whitespace) or document that the model re-run consumes the same normalized material the gate did.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether Pass-1/Pass-2 code-discovery/tool-fetch context is reconstructed and pinned for the replay (e.g. via the recorded distinct_fetches against a pinned codebase revision), or scope the tiers to plan-text-only findings so context drift cannot confound the measured noise floor.
evidence: pass1 records `distinct_fetches` (tool/target pairs) as part of the review's grounding, indicating Pass-1 grounds findings in fetched code, not only plan text
The plan's reconstruction target is 'at-review plan text' only; it is silent on freezing the discovery/tool-fetch context the finder/verifier actually saw
verify_findings takes a single `context` string; the plan supplies 'reconstructed plan text' as that context without addressing tool-derived context
findings.finding: The plan does not state whether Pass-1's code-discovery / tool-fetch context (beyond plan text) is reconstructable and frozen, yet Tier-1/Tier-2 replays feed the verifier/finder a reconstructed `context`; if discovery context is not fixed, the reproduction runs conflate verifier/finder noise with context drift.
findings.location: Approach, Tier 1 ('reconstructed plan text via the verify_findings(run_chunk=…) seam') and Tier 2; Invariant 4 (noise-aware acceptance)
scenarios: A Tier-1 reproduction run (unchanged questions) disagrees with stored answers not because of verifier noise but because the code the original review fetched has since changed or is not replayed, so the measured 'noise floor' is inflated and the acceptance band is mis-calibrated
A Tier-2 finder re-run over current code produces different findings than the original because discovery context differs, masking or fabricating a criterion-change effect

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile Tier-1/Tier-2 with ADR 0054 §2 (which rejects purpose-built LLM eval suites and bulk re-review sweeps as calibration instruments): explicitly invoke §2's prompt-development/regression-pinning carve-out, and state which tier is permitted for which change class (esp. that Pass-3 threshold/formula changes are calibration and must be justified by Tier-0 replay, not Tier-1/Tier-2).
evidence: Plan: 'Tier 1 — Pass-2 replay (Sonnet …). Re-run the verifier … Tier 2 — Pass-1 replay (Opus …). Re-run finders … on a fixed stratified sample (~20 tickets)'
Plan invariant 3 cites ADR 0054 only for offline-Tier-0 support: 'Consistent with ADR 0054 (the field corpus is the instrument)'

docs/adr/0054-...md §2: 'The following MUST NOT be required, planned, or commissioned … Purpose-built LLM eval suites … Bulk re-review sweeps — re-running review-plan / review-code across a corpus of tickets to observe how a candidate value would have scored.'
docs/adr/0054 §2 carve-out (uncited by the plan): 'It says nothing about evals used for their own purposes (prompt development, regression pinning of model behavior, capability checks).'
findings.finding: The plan cites ADR 0054 only as support for its offline-first invariant, but ADR 0054 §2 explicitly REJECTS 'purpose-built LLM eval suites' and 'bulk re-review sweeps — re-running review-plan/review-code across a corpus of tickets to observe how a candidate value would have scored' as calibration instruments; the plan's Tier-1 and Tier-2 are exactly those, and the Pass-3 threshold/formula assessment case is squarely calibration (ADR 0054's domain). The plan does not confront this tension or invoke ADR 0054 §2's carve-out for prompt-development/regression-pinning evals.
findings.location: Approach → Tier 1 / Tier 2; Non-negotiable invariant 3 ('Consistent with ADR 0054 … and with 6982's rejection of live A/B')
scenarios: A reviewer or operator asks why this epic commissions the very LLM re-review sweeps ADR 0054 §2 names as rejected; the plan's own citation of ADR 0054 as support makes the contradiction sharper.
A Pass-3 threshold change assessed via Tier-1/Tier-2 (rather than Tier-0 alone) — that is calibration, where ADR 0054's rejection is fully in force.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'ADR 0054 reconciliation' paragraph: Tier-0 is the ADR-0054-mandated corpus replay; Tier-1/Tier-2 are scoped strictly to Pass-2/Pass-1 PROMPT-and-question REGRESSION detection (§2's 'prompt development / regression pinning of model behavior' carve-out), never as the instrument for a threshold/formula calibration, which ADR 0054 restricts to Tier-0 replay + dogfooding.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the 6982 characterization (it rejected the OFFLINE counterfactual LLM batch baseline on cost and found it empirically unpopulated, not merely live A/B) and cite/differentiate criterion_effectiveness.py (story d8a5) as the closest prior art, stating what this harness adds over the shipped zero-LLM recorder.

Ticket 6982 close note: 'E2/E3 RESCOPED: … the expensive LLM batch baseline PERMANENTLY REJECTED on cost and superseded by story d8a5 (criterion_effectiveness.py, change #798); mining independently confirmed dead (~4 plan-v3 baselines vs the ~200 the counterfactual replay assumed).'
Ticket 6982 E3 described as 'counterfactual replay ~200 reviews' — an OFFLINE sweep, not live A/B.
docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/criterion_effectiveness.py exists (a shipped zero-LLM sidecar-native effectiveness recorder) — uncited by the plan.
findings.finding: The plan materially understates what epic 6982 (pastoral-aquatic-viper) rejected and omits its shipped superseding artifact. The plan says 6982 'rejected live A/B batches on cost'; the ticket shows 6982 permanently rejected the OFFLINE counterfactual LLM batch baseline (E3, '~200 reviews'), found batch-mining 'dead on its own terms' (~4 plan-v3 baselines vs ~200 assumed), and superseded it with a shipped zero-LLM standing effectiveness recorder (criterion_effectiveness.py, story d8a5) — the closest prior art to this harness, which the plan neither cites nor differentiates against.
findings.location: Context (¶1: 'the prior calibration epic (pastoral-aquatic-viper, 6982) rejected live A/B batches on cost and parked the human gold set')
scenarios: The author designs the Tier-2 baseline sample believing only live A/B was rejected, unaware the offline counterfactual replay was rejected on cost AND found empirically unpopulated for plan-v3.
criterion_effectiveness.py already answers 'is this criterion firing effectively?' at zero LLM cost; overlap with this harness's label-proxy metrics is unassessed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the plan_replay novelty vs the existing src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py prompt-eval framework (reuse vs new package, and why) and rebut 6982's 're-running the gate's own verifier is circular' lesson for Tier-2 (e.g. reliance on the outcome labels / noise-floor as construct-valid ground truth rather than self-adjudication).
evidence: Plan proposes 'New package src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/' without mentioning the sibling src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py.

src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py docstring: 'Prompt evaluation — regression detection + CI gating for git-canonical prompts … a git-tracked eval spec beside each prompt … dataset, thresholds, scorers … result gates CI.'

Ticket 6982 comment (candidate ADR): 'an adjudicator must be at least as capable … as the gate it judges, and re-running the gate's own verifier is circular — prefer CONSTRUCT-VALID ground truth … over LLM-adjudicated finding labels.'

Web prior art (retrieved): offline-first LLM eval/replay harnesses for 'did this prompt/model change make things better or worse?' with golden sets and CI regression gates are a well-trodden, off-the-shelf pattern (e.g. multiple public 'llm-eval-harness' projects).
findings.finding: The plan does not justify the novelty of an LLM-re-run harness (Tier-1/Tier-2) against two adjacent prior instruments it should confront: (a) the shipped in-repo prompt-eval framework src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py (git-canonical .rebar/evals/*.eval.yaml specs, golden datasets, deterministic-scorer gates, pinned-grader discipline, CI gating) — a 'did this prompt change make things better/worse' harness of exactly this shape — and (b) 6982's recorded methodological lesson that 're-running the gate's own verifier is circular'. This is an anti-repackaging / Rule-of-Three gap.
findings.location: Scope ('New package src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/'); Approach → Tier 1 / Tier 2
scenarios: A new evals/plan_replay/ tier-runner duplicates dataset/scorer/gate machinery that eval.py already provides for git-canonical prompts.

Tier-2 scores a candidate finder against finding sets produced by the same finder/verifier family, reproducing the circularity 6982 flagged, without the construct-valid ground truth that lesson recommends.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC #8 with the measured Opus-on-Bedrock caching failure: scope the 'caching confirmed active' requirement to the passes/models that actually cache (Sonnet/Pass-2), state Opus/Pass-1 as a known non-caching case, and route the caching gap to a SPIKE (or an explicit accepted-limitation) before committing the Tier-2 baseline.
evidence: AC #8: 'Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call of a run); verified from the usage log.'

infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md:146-147: 'Measured working: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6. Measured NOT caching: us./global. claude-opus-4-5-…' — caching is model-dependent and fails silently (cache_read=0).

tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py:8-9: 'us. AND global. opus-4-5 report cache_read=0 AND cache_write=0 while billing the full 4029 input tokens — caching fails SILENTLY and is model-dependent, not prefix-dependent.'
docs/adr/0059 lesson #10: 'Bedrock does not straightforwardly fix the opus caching failure … The opus-4-5 datapoint is never reconciled.'

src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:53-54 + docs/adr/0059:653-655: production 'frontier' (Pass-1) resolves to the opus inference profile; invariant 2 requires Pass-1 = frontier Opus on Bedrock — so AC #8's caching-active requirement lands on a model measured NOT to cache on Bedrock.
T3 evidence class: CONTRADICTED (the environment falsifies the asserted capability for Opus).
findings.finding: AC #8 asserts prompt caching will be 'confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call)', but the codebase's own MEASURED facts contradict this for the Pass-1 model the plan mandates: Opus on Bedrock reports cache_read=0/cache_write=0 (caching fails silently). Because invariant 2 forces frontier Opus via Bedrock only for Tier-2, AC #8 is unachievable as written for the Tier-2/Pass-1 path, and no SPIKE is routed to resolve the gap.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC #8 ('Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs'); Approach invariant 2 ('frontier Opus for Pass 1 … through Bedrock only')
scenarios: The Tier-2 baseline sample runs Opus on Bedrock; the usage log shows cache_read_tokens=0 on the second call; AC #8's verification step fails and the commissioning run cannot be signed off.
The 'reproduction run to measure verifier noise' (Tier-1, Sonnet) passes AC #8 while Tier-2 (Opus) cannot, so a single blanket AC hides a per-tier reality.
findings.suggested_fix: Split AC #8 by pass: require cache_read_tokens>0 on the second Tier-1 (Sonnet) call, and for Tier-2 (Opus) record the measured cache_read=0 as an accepted, documented Bedrock limitation (per ADR 0059 §7 / bedrock-access.md) rather than a pass condition; add a spike ticket to confirm whether any available Opus-class profile caches on Bedrock before sizing Tier-2 spend.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that the Tier-2 (Opus) cost estimate and ledger pre-flight are computed UNCACHED (because Opus does not cache on Bedrock per the measured evidence), so the hard-budget guard is grounded in real billing.
evidence: Approach Tier 2: 'Opus, ~$3.4/review uncached, plus a Tier-1 run on the new findings'.

Approach invariant 2 rationale: 'the mixed Bedrock+Anthropic fallback silently disables prompt caching and roughly doubles cost' — the plan treats caching as the cost lever, but the environment (bedrock-access.md, test_bedrock_provider.py) shows Opus-on-Bedrock never caches regardless of provider homogeneity.
T3 evidence class for the Opus caching assumption underlying the budget: CONTRADICTED for Opus, so an uncached Tier-2 estimate is the only sound basis.
findings.finding: The Tier-2 cost figure ('~$3.4/review uncached') and the $120 commissioning / $200-cap budget do not state whether the budget assumes prompt caching for Opus. Given Opus is measured NOT to cache on Bedrock (invariant 2's mandated Pass-1 path), the Tier-2 budget MUST be computed uncached; the plan should make that assumption explicit so the pre-flight cost estimate and the hard-cap guard are grounded in the real (non-caching) Opus billing rather than an unverified caching assumption.
findings.location: Approach, Tier 2 bullet ('Opus, ~$3.4/review uncached'); invariant 1 (hard budget, $120 commissioning / $200 cap)
scenarios: The pre-flight cost estimator applies a caching discount to Opus Tier-2 calls; actual Bedrock billing charges full input every call; projected spend understates real spend and the $200 hard cap is breached mid-run.
findings.suggested_fix: Annotate the Tier-2 cost bullet and invariant 1 to record 'Opus/Tier-2 priced uncached — Bedrock Opus caching is measured ineffective (ADR 0059 §7)'; reserve the caching discount for Tier-1/Sonnet only in the estimator.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how eval runs treat the production fallback chain: either DISABLE fallback for eval runs (Bedrock-only, fail loudly on a Bedrock error and abort/resume the run) or make the per-review model-parity guard operate PER RESULT (reject/quarantine any review whose recorded provider_provenance.ran_model is not the expected Bedrock id), so a mid-run failover cannot silently produce a heterogeneous, partially-uncached run.
evidence: Invariant 2 constrains only START/CONFIG time: the harness 'refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's provider_provenance.ran_model' and 'refuses to diff runs whose per-pass model ids differ' — nothing governs an in-run failover.

The production runner drives a FallbackModel chain: `should_fall_back` (src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:366) returns True for the availability classes AND `ResolutionClass.CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL`, i.e. it will move to the next configured candidate, which may be a NON-Bedrock provider (the mixed Bedrock+Anthropic chain the invariant itself warns 'silently disables prompt caching and roughly doubles cost').

The fallen-over model is what gets recorded: `provider_provenance['ran_model'] = ran_model` is set to the model that actually answered (src/rebar/llm/runner.py:712-713), so a mid-run failover yields per-review results whose ran_model legitimately differs from the Bedrock primary — inside one run, which the plan assumes is homogeneous.

The Tier-1 seam is the real verifier: `verify_findings(..., run_chunk=…)` (src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py:345) drives the production LLM path, so eval re-runs inherit the fallback chain unless the plan disables it.
findings.finding: Invariant 2 (model parity / homogeneous Bedrock chain) does not specify the eval run's behavior when a Bedrock LLM call FAILS MID-RUN and the production FallbackModel chain would fail over to a configured fallback target on a different provider/model — an unspecified fallback for a failed sub-step on the LLM surface the eval re-runs through.
findings.location: Approach → Invariant 2 (Model parity); Tier-1 and Tier-2 runners
scenarios: A Tier-1 reproduction run (the one that establishes the verifier noise floor) hits a transient Bedrock 5xx/throttle on review #400 of a batch; the chain fails over to Anthropic for that review only. Prompt caching silently disables for those calls (cost/measurement confound), and that review's ran_model is anthropic:… — so the run is no longer homogeneous, yet nothing refuses it because the START-time guard already passed.

The commissioning Tier-2 Opus baseline run partially fails over; the ledger/report shows a mix of Bedrock and non-Bedrock ran_model ids, contradicting AC7's 'ledger showing only Bedrock Opus/Sonnet ids'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Invariant 2: 'Eval runs configure NO fallback chain for the frontier/standard class (or set should_fall_back to reject every failover); a Bedrock call failure aborts the affected review and is retried on Bedrock, never relocated. Independently, every persisted eval result is validated PER REVIEW against the expected Bedrock per-pass model id via provider_provenance.ran_model, and any result whose ran_model differs is dropped from the run and flagged, not diffed.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile child 5d19 AC1 with parent AC3: either state the identity check runs corpus-wide with zero diffs, or explicitly name how reviews with non-current impact_model_version are handled (skipped-and-counted vs replayed) so the remainder is accounted for.
evidence: Child 5d19 AC1: 'tier0 --candidate current over the real corpus reports zero verdict flips against stored decisions for reviews whose impact_model_version matches current'
Parent AC3 verification clause: 'verified by replaying current code against itself with zero diffs'
Parent corpus holds ~4,300 sidecars spanning multiple impact_model_versions (v1 and v2 schemas noted in child 471c), so 'matches current' is a strict subset
findings.finding: Child 5d19's Tier-0 identity-check AC narrows the parent's AC3 self-replay population to reviews whose impact_model_version matches current, without naming the remainder; the parent AC3 verification is 'replaying current code against itself with zero diffs' over the corpus with no such restriction.
scenarios: A reviewer runs the identity check expecting zero diffs corpus-wide (per parent AC3) but the child only guarantees zero diffs on the current-version subset, leaving older-version reviews' identity behavior unspecified and potentially non-zero
Completion verifier for the parent epic checks AC3 against the whole corpus and the child's report only demonstrates the subset
findings.suggested_fix: Add to child 5d19 that non-current impact_model_version reviews are replayed under their historical model version (or explicitly skipped-and-counted in the report), so the identity check covers the whole corpus as parent AC3 requires.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign single ownership of the per-pass model-id ledger field: ledger (4c80) defines/writes the field; parity (efd4) supplies the resolved ids and validates them — state the seam explicitly in both children.
evidence: Child 4c80 ledger-row schema: '(run_id, tier, candidate, sample_n, started, finished, per-pass model ids, ...)' and AC1 'appears in the committed ledger with actual priced spend and per-pass model ids'
Child efd4 AC1: 'Every Tier-1/Tier-2 result and ledger row carries Bedrock model ids equal to the production class for that pass; checked by the ledger'
efd4 approach: 'every result row carries {pass: model_id}' — parity stamps the ids; ledger also records them
findings.finding: Ownership of the per-pass model-id ledger field is duplicated across children 4c80 (ledger) and efd4 (parity guard): both assert the ledger row carries production-class Bedrock model ids, with no stated division of who writes vs who validates the field.
scenarios: Both implementers write model-id-into-ledger-row logic, producing conflicting field names or double-writes
A parity-owned validation asserts a field the ledger owner formats differently, causing an integration mismatch at commissioning time
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify that parity.py produces the resolved per-pass Bedrock ids and passes them to ledger.py, which owns the ledger-row schema; efd4's AC then reads the ledger rather than independently writing them.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the child-decomposition ordering so the budget ledger (4c80) and model-parity guard (efd4) precede the Tier-1 (53ab) and Tier-2 (f1d6) harnesses, matching those harnesses' pre-flight/parity dependencies.
evidence: Parent child-decomposition: 'Tier-0 harness (3) -> Tier-1 harness (4) -> Tier-2 harness (5) -> budget ledger + model-parity guard ... (6, 7, 8)'
Child 53ab testing: 'a run whose pre-flight estimate exceeds the ledger allocation is refused before any call; a result with a non-standard-class model id is rejected at diff time'
Child f1d6 testing: 'a run is refused when the frontier model is not the Bedrock Opus id'
Child 4c80 provides ledger.reserve pre-flight; child efd4 provides parity.py refusal — both listed after Tier-1/Tier-2 in the decomposition
findings.finding: Ordering tension: the parent's child-decomposition sequences the ledger/parity children (6,7,8) AFTER Tier-1 (4) and Tier-2 (5), but the Tier-1 (53ab) and Tier-2 (f1d6) children's own ACs require the ledger's pre-flight/reserve seam and the parity guard to already exist ('a run whose pre-flight estimate exceeds the ledger allocation is refused before any call'; 'a run is refused when the frontier model is not the Bedrock Opus id').
scenarios: Implementing Tier-1/Tier-2 in the stated order forces the ledger and parity modules to be built (or stubbed) first, contradicting the written sequence

The Tier-1 commissioning run (a live spend, capped) cannot satisfy its budget-refusal and model-id-rejection ACs until 4c80 and efd4 land, so the ordering as written would block Tier-1's own acceptance
findings.suggested_fix: Reorder to: corpus (1) -> labels (2) -> ledger+parity (6,7,8) -> Tier-0 (3) -> Tier-1 (4) -> Tier-2 (5) -> protocol (9), or add explicit depends_on edges from 53ab/f1d6 to 4c80 and efd4.
